day_shape: 52 items: Trump blames Iran for Saudi East-West pipeline strike as Iraqi militias deny it, CENTCOM says 100 vessels redirected under 60-day 'steel wall' blockade, IRGC reports 5 killed in Sistan clash, and rial hits 2.3m/USD.

threads.label: Saudi pipeline strike blame
threads.summary: Trump said Iran was likely responsible for the drone attack that shut Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, while Jerusalem Post framed Iraqi Iran-backed militias as expanding regional reach. Iran International reported the Iraqi groups denied responsibility, though Baghdad has already dismissed a commander and closed Iran border crossings.

threads.label: US blockade and Gulf diplomacy
threads.summary: CENTCOM said it has redirected 100 commercial vessels in 60 days under the resumed 'steel wall' blockade of Iran, with USS Portland training in the Arabian Sea. Jerusalem Post reported a Monday Iran-Gulf meeting in Oman covering the Strait of Hormuz, and Araghchi held a call with Oman's foreign minister.

threads.label: Sistan security operation
threads.summary: Iran International reported heavy fighting in Saravan with dozens of security personnel killed or wounded per Haalvsh. IRGC Ground Forces via Defa Press and IRIB claimed five 'terrorists' were killed in a Sistan counter-terrorism operation.

threads.label: Yemen and Bab al-Mandab claims
threads.summary: Defa Press claimed 73 vessels passed Bab al-Mandab in two days after Yemen's army took control, and IRIB reported 210 Yemeni prisoners released from Saudi custody. Khamenei's office said the 'resistance front' achieved victories against 'American-Zionist' armies, while a Houthi official rejected Trump's claim of contact with Washington.

threads.label: Iran economy and internal pressure
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported the rial fell to 2.3 million per US dollar, and Iran International said state-linked Sepah Bank warned staff over pay protests and that a Bandar Abbas blogger was sentenced to death. Defa Press quoted Araghchi at BRICS pushing national-currency trade, and Rosatom said 47 of a planned 150 specialists have returned to Bushehr.

events.title_en: Smooth shipping passage after Yemen's army takes control of Bab al-Mandab. A source at the transport ministry of the Sanaa government in Yemen confirmed that vessel traffic through Bab al-Mandab is completely flowing. Referring to hostile countries seeking to internationalize aggression against Yemen through false claims, the source told Al-Masirah network: "In the past two days, 73 vessels have passed through Bab al-Mandab." The Yemeni source also reported that 36 vessels passed through Bab al-Mandab on 10 September and 37 vessels on 11 September. With these statements, he cast doubt on Saudi claims and those of their mercenaries who were expelled from the western coasts and Bab al-Mandab in recent days.
